card.name: Could/can before harm, and potentially hazardous
card.fires_on: The modal words "could" or "can" right after a drug or risk subject and before "cause harm", and the word "potentially" before "hazardous activities". Seen in warning sections of drug labels.

modes.label: Can/could cause harm
modes.description: The word can or could follows a drug, event or exposure and leads into a harm verb such as cause or be fatal.
modes.example: Advise patients of the risk of developing a seizure while receiving XTANDI and of engaging in any activity where sudden loss of consciousness<< could>> cause serious harm to themselves or others.

modes.label: Potentially hazardous
modes.description: The word potentially sits before hazardous in the driving and machinery warning.
modes.example: KORSUVA may impair the mental or physical abilities needed to perform<< potentially>> hazardous activities such as driving a car and

card.writes: It favors words of possibility and ease such as easily, potential and quickly, which fit a hedged risk statement.
card.plain: It marks hedge words like can, could and potentially that introduce a possible harm in a warning.
